answer: An agent marketplace requires every active identity to lock a separate bond of 100 tokens for 30 days before it can bid for jobs. Agents named yarrow, relic and atlas each tie up their own collateral; the contract prevents one deposit from backing multiple identities at once. An attacker running 10,000 fake agents must therefore immobilize one million tokens, paying financing costs throughout the lockup. Wealth can still buy influence, but identities are no longer free.
